precepts.text: These are the nations which the Lord left to prove Israel, that the generations might know to teach them war, at least such as before knew nothing thereof. He did not remove all the nations because he did not want us to skate through. We are in training now; in the kingdom we will be experts in everything. precepts.point: On postpartum: Deacon Malachiyah took hate for saying much of it is emotion, and the Bishop will take some too. Bearing children is the woman's makeup; the problem is a society with no support, sisters hating sisters, brothers hating women, a father barred from the maternity floor or fighting another man there, while the Edomite family fills the waiting room with jubilee. It is our job as men to build the midwives and the network so a sister brings forth fruit in a good way. Do not blame the children; a righteous child is a gift.

note.label: The Image of Dysfunction or the Image of God Which One Are You?

precepts.why:
Ezra saw the city of the kingdom with its narrow entrance, “like as if there were a fire on the right hand, and on the left a deep water”. That fire and deep water is the nations afflicting us. Judges makes the point about the nations: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan”.

He didn't get rid of all the nations. He said, no, I'm going to leave something there, because I don't want you to just skate through. You have to learn some things. If we did not have to be buffeted by our enemies, our journey would be quite smooth; but God put it that way because we messed up, and now we have to serve them, and they are going to make it hell for us to get the kingdom.

“Only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as before knew nothing thereof”. We didn't know about war before; now we know about war. We are getting the training now. When we get into the kingdom we are going to be experts in everything, bad upon bad, because we will have done it all and endured it all. That is what is going to make us perfect.

Captivity and persecution are hard and rough; nobody wants to go through these things. They can kill the body, but they cannot kill the spirit. They can do all kind of evil to my body physically, but when I come back, I'm going to hang your ass. That is the mindset you have to have: going for the kingdom regardless of what is thrown at you, to persevere between the fire on one side and the deep water on the other. “If then they that live labour not to enter these strait and vain things, they can never receive those that are laid up for them.”

note.label: Joshua 13: Much Land Yet to Be Possessed

precepts.why:
The nations were also left among Israel for a reason: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan; Only that the generations of the children of Israel might know, to teach them war, at the least such as before knew nothing thereof”.

The Most High left them to prove Israel, whether they would keep the commandments of the Most High, and so that the generations which had not known the wars of Canaan might be taught war. That is why very much land remained to be possessed. We all know what ended up happening with that proving, and it comes later on as we read.

precepts.text: All the families of the Canaanites that spread abroad, begotten of Canaan.
precepts.point: They were left to prove Israel, to know whether Israel would hearken unto the commandments of the Most High, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
Who are “all the Canaanites” the Most High left in the land to prove Israel? Genesis 10 lists the families. “And Canaan begat Sidon his firstborn, and Heth, And the Jebusite, and the Amorite, and the Girgasite, And the Hivite, and the Arkite, and the Sinite, And the Arvadite, and the Zemarite, and the Hamathite: and afterward were the families of the Canaanites spread abroad.”

So the Sidonians and the Hivites named among the nations that were left are themselves families of Canaan: Sidon was his firstborn, and the Hivite is one of his sons. All of these families spread abroad out of Canaan, and these are the people left in the land “to teach them war”, and to prove Israel, “to know whether they would hearken unto the commandments of the Lord, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.”

precepts.text: Seven nations greater and mightier than thou: make no covenant with them and no marriages with them, for they will turn away thy son from following me.
precepts.point: Going out to battle against horses and chariots and people more than thou, Israel was told, be not afraid of them, for the Most High is with thee. He constantly repeats these things because he knew we were going to be a stubborn and rebellious people, and he wants us to acknowledge him and only him. Instead Israel did evil, forgat the Most High, and served Baalim and the groves.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
Stop and read who Israel is dwelling among: “the Canaanites, Hittites, and Amorites, and Perizzites, and Hivites, and Jebusites.” Are those not the same people the Most High said to utterly destroy? Deuteronomy 7 names them: “the Hittites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, seven nations greater and mightier than thou.” And the commandment was, “thou shalt smite them, and utterly destroy them; thou shalt make no covenant with them, nor shew mercy unto them.” But we are dwelling among them.

The law said it plainly about the marriages too: “Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.” Judges 3 records the exact opposite: “they took their daughters to be their wives, and gave their daughters to their sons, and served their gods.”

The reason was given beforehand: “For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.” That is precisely what happened. Israel “forgat the Lord their God, and served Baalim and the groves.”

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
The law of war opens with courage: “When thou goest out to battle against thine enemies, and seest horses, and chariots, and a people more than thou, be not afraid of them: for the Lord thy God is with thee, which brought thee up out of the land of Egypt.”

Israel had no reason to leave these nations standing and dwell among them. Even against horses and chariots and a people more than thou, the Most High was with them. He constantly repeats these things because he knew we were going to be a stubborn and rebellious people, and he wants us to acknowledge him and only him. Instead Israel did evil, forgat the Most High, and served Baalim and the groves.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
The law of war made a different stipulation for far off cities than for these people. For the far cities: “When thou comest nigh unto a city to fight against it, then proclaim peace unto it. And it shall be, if it make thee answer of peace, and open unto thee, then it shall be, that all the people that is found therein shall be tributaries unto thee, and they shall serve thee.” That is just what we read the tribes doing with the Canaanites, putting them to tribute.

If the city would not make peace, “thou shalt besiege it: And when the Lord thy God hath delivered it into thine hands, thou shalt smite every male thereof with the edge of the sword.”

But that was the rule for far off cities. For the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites and Jebusites that Israel is now dwelling among, there was no offer of peace and no tribute; read on to verse 16.

precepts.text: But of the cities of these people thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth, that they teach you not to do after all their abominations.
precepts.point: Going out to battle against horses and chariots and people more than thou, Israel was told, be not afraid of them, for the Most High is with thee. He constantly repeats these things because he knew we were going to be a stubborn and rebellious people, and he wants us to acknowledge him and only him. Instead Israel did evil, forgat the Most High, and served Baalim and the groves.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
Here is the stipulation for the very people Israel dwelt among: “But of the cities of these people, which the Lord thy God doth give thee for an inheritance, thou shalt save alive nothing that breatheth: But thou shalt utterly destroy them; namely, the Hittites, and the Amorites, the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; as the Lord thy God hath commanded thee.” Total destruction, not peace and not tribute.

The reason is the very thing Judges 3 records happening: “That they teach you not to do after all their abominations, which they have done unto their gods; so should ye sin against the Lord your God.” Israel saved them alive, dwelt among them, married their daughters, “and served their gods.” The children of Israel “did evil in the sight of the Lord, and forgat the Lord their God, and served Baalim and the groves”, exactly the sin the commandment was given to prevent.

precepts.text: The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.
precepts.point: The Most High delivered Chushan-rishathaim into Othniel's hand, and the land had rest forty years, until Othniel the son of Kenaz died.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
Othniel “judged Israel, and went out to war”, because “The Lord is a man of war: the Lord is his name.” The spirit of the Lord came upon him, and a man with that spirit judges and goes to war.

That answers those who ask, when we are out on the streets teaching, where are your women. They are not at war; the Lord is a man of war. And it answers our people today who say, you can't judge me: the spirit of the Most High came upon Othniel and he judged Israel.

precepts.text: We do not war after the flesh; the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds.
precepts.point: The Most High delivered Chushan-rishathaim into Othniel's hand, and the land had rest forty years, until Othniel the son of Kenaz died.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
For those who do not think we are at war now: “though we walk in the flesh, we do not war after the flesh.” It is a spiritual war, but we are still nonetheless at war.

“For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but mighty through God to the pulling down of strong holds.” The weapon of our warfare today is this Bible, mighty through God, “Casting down imaginations, and every high thing that exalteth itself against the knowledge of God, and bringing into captivity every thought to the obedience of Christ”, exposing all the lies on the earth.

Othniel went out to war with the sword and the Lord delivered Chushan-rishathaim into his hand. We go out to war with the word, and it is the same Lord, the man of war, who gives the victory.

precepts.text: Your terror is fallen upon us; as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt. The same nations whose hearts melted are now strengthened against disobedient Israel.
precepts.point: Eglon gathers the children of Ammon and Amalek, smites Israel, and possesses the city of palm trees, and the children of Israel serve Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

precepts.why:
Wait a minute: it says “the Lord strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel.” Compare that with Joshua. Rahab told the spies, “I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you.”

The nations had heard what the Most High did for us: “how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed.” And the effect was, “as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you: for the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.”

The same nations whose hearts melted are now strengthened against Israel, and the Most High is the one strengthening them, “because they had done evil in the sight of the Lord.” When we kept his commandments the heathen fainted before us; when we broke them, he made Eglon strong enough to smite Israel and hold us eighteen years.

precepts.text: The Lord left nations to prove Israel, that the generations which had not known all the wars of Canaan might be taught war, and to know whether Israel would hearken unto the commandments which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.
precepts.point: Notice it says to defend Israel. Israel was in the land, but do not forget that the Lord had left nations among us, so the judges had to defend the people.

note.label: Judges 10: Go and Cry unto the Gods Which Ye Have Chosen

precepts.why:
Notice it says Tola arose “to defend Israel”. Israel was in the land, but do not forget that the Lord had left nations among us: “Now these are the nations which the Lord left, to prove Israel by them, even as many of Israel as had not known all the wars of Canaan”. He left them “to teach them war”, that the generations which had not known the wars of Canaan might learn it, and “to know whether they would hearken unto the commandments of the Lord, which he commanded their fathers by the hand of Moses.”

Those nations were the five lords of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that dwelt in mount Lebanon. With them left in the land, the judges had to defend the people; that is why Tola’s twenty and three years are described as defending Israel.

precepts.text: Eglon's servants saw the doors of the parlour locked and said, Surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber, and tarried till they were ashamed; covering the feet is the scripture's phrase for relieving yourself.
precepts.point: Saul went into the cave to cover his feet: that means he was in there relieving himself. See the vulnerable position Saul was in, and yet David spared his life; that is why David could say, thou wast delivered into my hand, but I did not take thy life.

note.label: 1 Samuel 24: David Spares Saul in the Cave at Engedi

precepts.why:
When Eglon's servants came and found “the doors of the parlour were locked, they said, Surely he covereth his feet in his summer chamber. And they tarried till they were ashamed.” Covering the feet is the scripture's phrase for relieving yourself.

So when “Saul went in to cover his feet”, he was in that cave relieving himself. Coming out of the prior chapters, Saul was hunting after David to kill him: he “took three thousand chosen men out of all Israel, and went to seek David and his men upon the rocks of the wild goats”, while “David and his men remained in the sides of the cave.”

See the vulnerable position Saul was in, and yet David spared his life. That is why David could say, thou wast delivered into my hand, but I did not take thy life.

note.label: 1 Kings 9: The Most High Appears to Solomon a Second Time

precepts.why:

Those same nations, their children “that were left after them in the land”, are the ones Solomon put under a tribute of bondservice, while the children of Israel served as his men of war, his captains and the rulers of his chariots and horsemen.

They slay of Moab about ten thousand men, all lusty men of valour, and not a man escapes.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

points: So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel, and the land had rest fourscore years.

note.label: Judges 3: Nations Left to Prove Israel

points: After Ehud was Shamgar the son of Anath, which slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad; and he also delivered Israel.
